mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over a 3-month period signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPI increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals robust demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over a 3-month period signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, the combined effect signals tightening monetary conditions and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in a month, the combined effect signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the interaction effect between PAYEMS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) increasing by more than 1% in a quarter signals robust consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1%, signals a supply-side contraction with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 1% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the interaction effect between INDPRO decreases and FEDFUNDS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
